    Vennerian Cable & Knot¶

    [!INFO] Cable by Cable, Knot by Knot — The Sea's Own Measure The salt-rope measure of the Vennerian Trade Republic — counted on deck, knotted in rope, and taxed at the Vennerian Channel gates.

    Base Units¶

    Born on the roll of a ship. Vennerian measure is practical — a unit must be usable with wet hands, in wind, at night. Every Vennerian vessel carries a standard Cable rope (100 Fathoms, tarred, knotted) and a Knot-log (chip-log on 47-foot-3-inch line). Harbourmasters at Vennerian Channel keep the master Cable in a copper-lined vault; cheating it is piracy.

    Domain Unit Relation Notes
    Length Inch base as Erisian — ship's inch
    Foot 12 Inches Vennerian Foot 30.8 cm — ship-foot, slightly longer
    Fathom 6 Feet arm-span — sounding line, 1.85 m. Two fathoms and a half, sir
    Cable 100 Fathoms the Cable — 185.2 m. Standard rope length. 10 Cables = 1 Nautical Mile
    Nautical Mile 10 Cables 1,852 m — sea mile. The Channel is 12 Nautical Miles long
    League 3 Nautical Miles 5.556 km — watch-to-watch sailing
    Speed Knot 1 Nautical Mile per hour chip-log count — knots paid out per glass (28 seconds). She makes 8 knots
    Depth Fathom as above lead-line. Marked by rags: white at 5, red at 10, blue at 15
    Weight Ounce base as Erisian
    Pound 16 Ounces ship-pound 454 g — ballast pound
    Stone 14 Pounds crew provision stone
    Hundredweight 8 Stone cargo hundred
    Ton 20 Hundredweight register ton — 40 cubic feet of cargo space, not weight. Vennerian trick
    Volume Pint base as Erisian
    Gallon 8 Pints ship gallon
    Barrel 36 Gallons water barrel — one barrel per man per fortnight
    Butt 2 Barrels great cask
    Tun 252 Gallons same as Erisian — for wine duty at the Channel

    Shanty mnemonics: Six feet a fathom, a hundred the cable, ten the mile — pay at the gate if ye be able.

    Who Uses¶

    The maritime empire of the Vennerian Trade Republic — sailors, pilots, chandlers, rope-makers, and every soul who pays the Vennerian Channel toll. Dominant at Beast's Bay, Mia Checkpoint, Goishi, Vennerian Channel, Love of the Sea, New Venner, Johannstadt, Sua, Eribel, and Demon's Horn traders who translate Cables to Miles with a scowl.

    Inland Vennerian merchants still use Erisian Standard Miles on land — a Vennerian will say twelve Miles by road, seven by sea — pay the sea rate.

    Conversion Notes¶

    • To Erisian Standard: 1 Vennerian Cable = 607.6 Erisian Feet (100 Fathoms). 1 Nautical Mile = 6,076 Erisian Feet = 1.15 Erisian Miles. 1 Vennerian League = 3.45 Erisian Miles. Channel tollboards show both; the Vennerian column is larger.
    • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Cable = 6.61 Dwarven Stone — dwarven harbor pilots at Dwarvengor keep a conversion slate nailed to the pier.
    • To Anosi Ledger-Weight: Weight is identical to Erisian/Anosi; length is not. Vennerian factors quote freight in register Tons (volume) while Anosi factors quote in weight Tons — the discrepancy is a perennial lawsuit at Beast's Bay.
    • Knot discipline: A Knot is speed only; landsmen who say knots per hour are corrected, loudly, with rope.
    • Romanium: Romanium is assayed in Erisian Grains for treaty, but Vennerian manifests list it in ship-pounds — 1 ship-pound Romanium = 1.002 Erisian Pounds, and Venner pockets the sliver on every ingot through the Channel.

    Flavor¶

    Vennerian measure smells of tar. A Cable is not an abstraction — it is a rope you can hold, that has a weight, that frays and is replaced, that you paid for. Young deckhands learn fathom, cable, mile by hauling the sounding lead, not by reading. The chip-log glass is 28 seconds because the old glass-maker counted one-one-thousand wrong and Venner decided tradition outweighed arithmetic.

    The Ducat is backed by the Channel toll; the Cable is backed by the Channel itself — you cannot argue with a ditch someone dug and dares you to avoid.

    At Beast's Bay the trilingual board reads: 10 Cables : 1 Sea Mile : 1.15 Land Miles — PAY HERE.
